title: Agent evaluation in Copilot Studio: how agents are tested, what the tests cost and who can limit them
summary: Hold: the proposed automation for an agent's monthly spending limit is documented only for an unspecified environment resource, not for a Copilot Studio agent. The evaluation behaviour, billing distinction and documented disagreement about blocking the connector are otherwise supported, with small qualifications and citation corrections needed.

claims.claim: An existing data policy's connector Block action is reached through Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Assign connectors > connector > three dots > Block.
claims.quote: Select Next. The Add an environment page appears. ... Select Next. The Assign connectors page appears.
claims.fix: Include the intervening scope-selection page: 'Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Add an environment > Assign connectors > connector > three dots > Block'. The omitted environment selection is a target-selection step, not a wrong route.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy with PolicyName, Classification and Connectors assigns connectors to a policy's data group.
claims.quote:
Add-ConnectorsToPolicy
    [-PolicyName] <String>
    [-Classification] <String>
    [-Connectors] <Object[]>

claims.claim: The environment tenant-capacity draw setting is at Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: Under Products, select Copilot Studio, and then select Manage Copilot Credits. ... Under Capacity overages, select or clear Draw from the available capacity in my tenant

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes an environment's allocation and tenant-capacity enforcement rule.
claims.quote: Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put ... -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"

claims.claim: An agent's monthly limit and Stop usage setting are reached through Licensing > Copilot Studio > Manage Agents > agent > Set limit > Stop usage.
claims.quote: Select Manage Agents. ... Select the agent, and then select Set limit. ... Turn on Stop usage if the agent should be turned off when it reaches the limit.

claims.claim: The Resource Threshold PUT operation is the API equivalent of setting a Copilot Studio agent's monthly Copilot Credit limit and Stop usage.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform API agent monthly limit resource threshold resourceId MCSMessages stopIfOverCapacity; "Copilot Studio" "agent" "upsert" "threshold". Read Resource Threshold REST reference, pac licensing and both cited capacity-management pages; none maps an agent to this resource.
claims.fix: Set controls[2].api to null and replace its API-related note with 'The Resource Threshold API documents thresholds for an environment resource, but Microsoft does not document here how to use it for a Copilot Studio agent's monthly limit.' Keep the existing question about whether evaluation runs count. The generic operation's existence does not establish that it changes this agent control.

claims.claim: In the Microsoft Copilot harness experience, a maker opens the agent, selects Evaluate, selects an evaluation and selects Evaluate to start it.
claims.quote: Open your agent in Copilot Studio. ... Select the Evaluate tab. ... In the Evaluation dropdown, select the evaluation you want to run. ... Select Evaluate to start the evaluation.

claims.claim: POST https://api.powerplatform.com/copilotstudio/environments/{EnvironmentId}/bots/{BotId}/api/makerevaluation/testsets/{TestSetId}/run?api-version=2024-10-01 starts an evaluation against a test set.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness. ... Purpose: Run an evaluation for a test set by using the test set's id.
claims.fix: Add to the row note: 'The UI route is for the Microsoft Copilot harness preview; the cited evaluation API documentation describes the standard harness.' Do not imply that this API is documented for both experiences.

claims.claim: A dedicated tenant or environment switch that turns agent evaluation off is not documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio disable agent evaluation tenant environment setting Power Platform API evaluation switch; "agent evaluation" "Organization" "Is" "enabled" Dataverse. Opened evaluation intro, evaluation REST API and data-policy pages; no dedicated switch found.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio's data-policy page says blocking the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector prevents authenticated evaluation runs.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from adding event triggers to their agents or running automated evaluations by using an authenticated account, configure a data policy that blocks the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector.

claims.claim: Power Platform's connector-classification page lists Microsoft Copilot Studio among connectors that data policies cannot block.
claims.quote: The following connectors can't be blocked by using data policies. ... Microsoft 365 Groups Mail (Preview) | Microsoft Copilot Studio

claims.where: Risks and limits: The data policy route may not hold
claims.claim: The connector-classification page says advanced connector policies can restrict the otherwise nonblockable certified connectors.
claims.quote: ACP uses a strict allowlist model and can restrict any certified connector, including the nonblockable connectors listed in this article.

claims.claim: The TenantPool enforcement rule in the allocation request controls whether the environment draws on tenant capacity.
claims.quote: The Draw from the available capacity in my tenant option in the admin center maps to the TenantPool enforcement rule

claims.claim: Clearing tenant-capacity draw stops prepaid consumption at the environment's allocation but does not stop consumption through a linked pay-as-you-go plan.
claims.quote: When you clear this option, the environment doesn't draw from unallocated prepaid capacity ... If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.claim: An agent-level monthly Copilot Credit limit with Stop usage turns the agent off when it reaches the limit.
claims.quote: Turn on Stop usage if the agent should be turned off when it reaches the limit.
claims.fix: Add to the row note: 'Limits are not applied instantly: an agent can continue to respond after reaching its limit. An agent's monthly limit does not stop the agent flows it calls.' These qualifications are in https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-copilot-studio-copilot-credits-capacity#manage-monthly-consumption-limits-for-copilot-studio-agents; the row should not read as an instantaneous spending guarantee.

claims.claim: The threshold reference describes an environment resource, rather than naming agents, and lists limit and stopIfOverCapacity in the request body.
claims.quote: Create or update the resource threshold for an environment resource. ... Request Body ... limit ... stopIfOverCapacity

claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly document whether the per-agent monthly limit counts or stops evaluation runs.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio evaluation runs agent monthly limit stop usage evaluations; "Copilot Studio" "evaluations" "monthly" "limit" "stop". Read harness cost-management, capacity-management and Resource Threshold pages; none explicitly resolves evaluation-run counting.
